units: Erub. III, 1 הנודר מן המ׳ וכ׳ he who vows abstinence from mazon (nourishment) is permitted to partake of water and salt.
Ib. 30ᵃ; Ber. 35ᵇ מים ומלח הוא דלא איקרי מ׳ וכ׳ only water and salt are not called mazon, but all other food is included in mazon; Gen. R. s. 94, beg.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 8:2">Erub. VIII, 2</cite> <he>מ׳ ב׳ סעודות</he> food for two meals.
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 8:8">Ber. VIII, 8</cite> <he>לאחר המ׳</he> for the after-meal (dessert).

<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 8:8">Ib.</cite> <he>מברך על המ׳</he> he says the grace after meal. Ib. 5 <he>נר ומ׳ וכ׳</he> the benediction for the light, then for the meal, then for the spices &c.; <cite ref="Pesachim 103a">Pes. 103ᵃ</cite>.—<he>ברכת המ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="B01292"><he>בְּרָכָה</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 6:8">Ber. VI, 8</cite> <he>והוא מְזוֹנוֹ</he> and this was his meal.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 15:3:8">Y. Yeb. XV, 14ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>מ׳ האשה והבנות</he> the alimentation of wife and daughters (after a man’s death). Ib. VII, 8ᵃ bot. <he>מ׳ הבנות מדבריהן</he> the obligation to support the daughters from a man’s estate is a Rabbinical enactment; a. fr.—Pl. <he>מְזוֹנוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Berakhot 35b:17">Ber. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>בורא מיני מ׳</he> (abbrev. <he>במ״מ</he>) (Blessed be he) who created various kinds of food.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 4:6">Keth. IV, 6</cite> <he>חייב במ׳ בתו</he> bound to support his daughter.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 11:2">Ib. XI, 2</cite> <he>אין לה מ׳</he> she cannot claim alimentation.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 11:3">Ib. 3</cite> <he>למ׳ מכרתי</he> I have sold (a portion of my widowhood) for my support.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 12:2">Ib. XII, 2</cite> <he>הבעל נותן לה מ׳ … דמי מ׳</he> her husband supports her, and they (the heirs) must give her the equivalent of her support; a. fr.
